summary: Yoshifumi Mizuno works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, and had a long career at Komazawa University as a lecturer in 1971 and professor in 2001.
Yoshihiko Amino was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950). He held posts at Nagoya University (~1973–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1993).
Yoshihiko Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and positions at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (both attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). His posts include part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and researcher at Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Yoshihiro Hayashi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, he was attested as a professor at Ritsumeikan University and as a part-time lecturer at Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1991–1999) and president (2001) at Taisho University.

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, later holding posts at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who held posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held posts at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), served as president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and taught at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).
Yoshinobu Sakade was a Sinologist and philosopher. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1962) under Mitsuji Fukunaga and held a post at Kansai University from around 1970 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy and religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe and held positions as professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1978–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and under Paul Demiéville (~1961–1963), and served as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1949 to 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and held a post at Tohoku University from around 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Bernard Frank. He held posts at CNRS (~1973–2012) and Kyoto University (~2012–2017).

Yoshiro Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher educated at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University (1965–1972), the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1980–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University (1955–1977), and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1986).
Yoshito S. Hakeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor and associate professor at Columbia University, remaining there until 1983.
